content.text: I verified the Linux and macOS release assets and found two important caveats. Squiggle’s media-related projects still target Windows, and BeeBEEP’s beta download page lists its packages as “Coming soon.” I’ll carry both distinctions into the notes.

text(await tools.exec_command({workdir:"/Users/kingsonwu/programming/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/.worktrees/req-029",cmd:`cat > tmp/req-029-lan-sources.md <<'EOF'
# REQ-029 first-party LAN messenger evidence

Checked 23 November 2026 against the five products linked in the historical REQ-029 references and the claims in the working landscape, analysis and peer-evidence notes. Release pages and expanded asset lists establish publication. Tagged code establishes implementation in a particular source revision. Project documentation establishes what maintainers describe. This was a desk review. Installation, interoperability, performance, security assurance and user demand remain untested.

## LANChat — cap153/LANChat

- **Published.** GitHub labels v0.1.5 (18 June 2026, \`6d68944\`) Latest. Its assets include a Windows x64 desktop executable, Linux amd64 DEB/RPM, an ARM64 Android APK, a Linux amd64 headless web archive and a Windows web executable. The release notes identify IP-based manual discovery, a heartbeat reply, notifications including Web, manual file acceptance and the LANClaw integration. LANClaw is a separately operated Pi-powered bot. A native macOS product release is unverified. [v0.1.5 release](https://github.com/cap153/LANChat/releases/tag/v0.1.5) · [Asset list](https://github.com/cap153/LANChat/releases/expanded_assets/v0.1.5) · [LANClaw project](https://github.com/cap153/LANClaw)
- **Architecture and browser boundary.** The Rust backend has a Tauri 2 native entry and a standalone \`lanchat-web\` entry. Both initialize the SQLite schema through shared code and own discovery and the local peer identity. Desktop and standalone starts can use the same database layout, with path selection depending on the entry point and configuration. The standalone process serves vanilla HTML/CSS/JS through Axum, starts UDP broadcast/multicast and handles native peer traffic. Browser JavaScript calls the host's HTTP API and subscribes to \`/ws\`. Peer transport includes TCP and the browser uploads file chunks through HTTP. The browser operates the host's peer identity, using its database and reachability. [Binary targets](https://github.com/cap153/LANChat/blob/v0.1.5/src-tauri/Cargo.toml#L12) · [Standalone entry](https://github.com/cap153/LANChat/blob/v0.1.5/src-tauri/src/server_main.rs#L23) · [Native entry](https://github.com/cap153/LANChat/blob/v0.1.5/src-tauri/src/lib.rs#L99) · [SQLite initialization](https://github.com/cap153/LANChat/blob/v0.1.5/src-tauri/src/db.rs#L129) · [Browser API](https://github.com/cap153/LANChat/blob/v0.1.5/src/js/api.js) · [WebSocket client](https://github.com/cap153/LANChat/blob/v0.1.5/src/js/app.js#L498)
- **Web/PWA gaps.** The v0.1.5 router binds plain HTTP on all interfaces, with permissive CORS and host settings, send and history routes. Scoped per-visitor authorization is absent from that router. The separate Android media token covers a local media path. The browser shell and source scan yielded no install manifest, registered service worker, browser-owned peer transport or offline messaging when the host is unreachable. Treat Web as a shipped, host-dependent browser client. A browser's generic site shortcut and installable/offline app support are separate claims. Browser notification support also depends on origin, permissions and browser behavior. [Tagged router](https://github.com/cap153/LANChat/blob/v0.1.5/src-tauri/src/web_server.rs#L95-L140) · [Android local media handler](https://github.com/cap153/LANChat/blob/v0.1.5/src-tauri/src/web_server.rs#L1700) · [Tagged browser shell](https://github.com/cap153/LANChat/blob/v0.1.5/src/index.html) · [Current browser shell](https://github.com/cap153/LANChat/blob/95a645c90823c20d64e68044dc441ee3a7a9705d/src/index.html)
- **Routing and recovery.** v0.1.5 release notes cover manual IP addition across VLAN/WireGuard and reciprocal discovery by heartbeat. The explicit hostname/DNS lookup with a cache is present in inspected main at \`95a645c\` and belongs in a source-level claim. Existing routes and firewall permission still govern connectivity. v0.1.4 documents reconnect resend. Tagged discovery invokes the sender's pending-record resend and tagged messaging can read and resend an available local file. This evidence covers retry from a reachable sender and leaves independent byte custody after sender shutdown unverified. [v0.1.5 discovery](https://github.com/cap153/LANChat/blob/v0.1.5/src-tauri/src/network/discovery.rs#L83) · [Pinned main DNS code](https://github.com/cap153/LANChat/blob/95a645c90823c20d64e68044dc441ee3a7a9705d/src-tauri/src/network/discovery.rs#L110-L153) · [v0.1.4 release](https://github.com/cap153/LANChat/releases/tag/v0.1.4) · [Resend implementation](https://github.com/cap153/LANChat/blob/v0.1.5/src-tauri/src/network/messaging.rs#L500)
- **Media and mobile.** v0.1.1 documents streaming file transfer and adaptive chunks. v0.1.2 documents Android share-in/share-out, desktop/Web drop and paste, and image previews. v0.1.3 adds Android tap-to-open and permission-dependent preview. v0.1.4 adds pasting clipboard images. The later main README describes the Android Storage Access Framework picker and persisted URI/descriptor paths. Main marks group chat in progress. The cited release notes and inspected source support image/file workflows. Live voice, video and screen sharing have no verified implementation or release here. [v0.1.1](https://github.com/cap153/LANChat/releases/tag/v0.1.1) · [v0.1.2](https://github.com/cap153/LANChat/releases/tag/v0.1.2) · [v0.1.3](https://github.com/cap153/LANChat/releases/tag/v0.1.3) · [v0.1.4](https://github.com/cap153/LANChat/releases/tag/v0.1.4) · [Pinned main README](https://github.com/cap153/LANChat/blob/95a645c90823c20d64e68044dc441ee3a7a9705d/README.md)
- **Mesh Talk applicability.** Useful precedents include one-link access to a running host, Android share-sheet file intake and recovery from peer address changes. A Mesh Talk browser experiment needs an explicit host lifecycle, separate guest authority with expiry and revocation, and a trusted origin. A paired browser/PWA would additionally need its own identity, storage and lifecycle design. Existing manual endpoints and authorized post-office custody already cover different parts of routing and recovery. [Routed networks](../docs/help/topics/routed-networks.md) · [Files](../docs/help/topics/send-files.md) · [Post offices](../docs/help/topics/post-offices.md)

## BLIP — krwg/blip

- **Published and prerelease.** GitHub labels v2.0.3 Morse (27 July 2026, \`9dd440f\`) Latest. v2.0.5 is a beta prerelease. v3.0.0 Spark (2 November 2026, \`d887af1\`) is a published prerelease with downloadable assets even though its tagged changelog calls the beta unreleased. The v2.0.3 and v3.0.0 asset lists contain Windows setup and portable executables, Intel and Apple Silicon macOS DMG/ZIP and Linux x64 AppImage/DEB. Groups are described as beta even on v2.0.3. The static landing page displays the older v2.0.0 version. [Releases](https://github.com/krwg/blip/releases) · [v2.0.3 assets](https://github.com/krwg/blip/releases/expanded_assets/v2.0.3) · [v3.0.0 assets](https://github.com/krwg/blip/releases/expanded_assets/v3.0.0) · [v3.0.0 changelog](https://github.com/krwg/blip/blob/v3.0.0/CHANGELOG.md) · [Landing page](https://krwg.github.io/blip/)
- **Native architecture and Web/PWA.** Electron main owns UDP broadcast, auxiliary mDNS and peer TCP for chat, control and SDP/ICE signaling. Preload exposes native functionality to the Vite renderer over IPC. WebRTC media runs in the Electron renderer, with dedicated call windows. Repository Pages publishes the static \`docs\` showcase. The inspected trees and releases yielded no standalone web messaging client, shipped PWA, browser-only discovery or mobile artifact. On an ordinary LAN/VPN path, usable discovery, TCP signaling and ICE/media are separate reachability checks. [Tagged architecture](https://github.com/krwg/blip/blob/v2.0.3/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md#processes--windows) · [IPC bridge](https://github.com/krwg/blip/blob/v2.0.3/preload.cjs#L301) · [Pages workflow](https://github.com/krwg/blip/blob/v2.0.3/.github/workflows/pages.yml#L26)
- **Media and topology.** Tagged v2.0.3 supports native 1:1 voice/video and live screen capture. The older group call window manages peer-to-peer WebRTC connections among participants. The group voice-channel path uses a host-centered star. Its host creates per-peer mixes and returns mix-minus audio. The documented 720p/1080p settings are capture targets. Throughput, delivered frame rate, simultaneous channel size, system audio behavior, platform parity and host-loss recovery require runtime evidence. A user can configure STUN/TURN for new calls, with an empty ICE server list when the option is disabled. [Tagged README](https://github.com/krwg/blip/blob/v2.0.3/README.md#en-features) · [Calls and media](https://github.com/krwg/blip/blob/v2.0.3/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md#calls--media) · [Voice-channel mixer](https://github.com/krwg/blip/blob/v2.0.3/renderer/voice-channel.js#L206-L295) · [Group call peer implementation](https://github.com/krwg/blip/blob/v2.0.3/renderer/group-call.js#L290) · [ICE configuration](https://github.com/krwg/blip/blob/v2.0.3/shared/ice-servers.js#L25)
- **Compatibility and optional route.** Tagged v2.0.3 documents signed modern discovery and an authenticated handshake followed by AES-GCM transport for modern peers. Legacy protocol peers use an explicitly labeled plaintext TCP path. The v3.0.0 prerelease documents optional SteamLAN with a signed-in Steam desktop account and possible Valve relay fallback. The documented tunnel covers discovery/chat/signaling and leaves media to WebRTC. Scope the account-free LAN path and the Steam-assisted path separately. Peer compatibility and privacy guarantees need mode-specific testing. [Mesh handshake](https://github.com/krwg/blip/blob/v2.0.3/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md#mesh-handshake) · [SteamLAN prerelease architecture](https://github.com/krwg/blip/blob/v3.0.0/docs/STEAM-LAN.md)
- **Files and collaboration.** Tagged architecture documents inline attachments, JPEG images, individual chunked offers for large group files, a configurable 1–100 GB cap and BEACON multi-peer seeded distribution. The cap is a configured limit. BEACON can fetch from live seeders with chunks, and recipient authorization, retention and availability differ from a managed store-and-forward mailbox. The tagged README also documents Mesh Pulse auto-ping, clipboard modes (off, active DM, trusted peers) and the optional group-independent Signal Corps workspace, with some tools gated by MESH+. [File, BEACON and clipboard design](https://github.com/krwg/blip/blob/v2.0.3/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md#file-transfer) · [Tagged README](https://github.com/krwg/blip/blob/v2.0.3/README.md#en-features) · [Signal Corps](https://github.com/krwg/blip/blob/v2.0.3/README.md#en-signal-corps)
- **Mesh Talk applicability.** Compare capture/stop controls, call status and separate discovery/signaling/media diagnostics with existing experimental 1:1 calls. Small voluntary group voice needs an explicit topology and host-disconnect criteria. Compare per-person transfer states with Mesh Talk's existing file flow. Preserve the meanings of retained message, saved file and authorized offline source. [Mesh Talk calls](../docs/help/topics/calls.md) · [Delivery](../docs/help/topics/delivery.md) · [Network contract](../docs/network-design-reference.md)

## LAN Messenger — lanmessenger/lanmessenger

- **Production version and assets.** The live official site and GitHub Latest agree on v1.3.27 (21 November 2026, \`6bf6f9c\`). The historical 1.3.9 snapshot is stale. A search excerpt also showed 1.3.21, which the live site and asset list supersede. The site offers Windows x64 EXE, Apple Silicon/Intel DMGs and Linux amd64 DEB/RPM. GitHub additionally lists an Arch package and SHA-256 manifest. The site's portable Windows entry is in the 1.2.x archive. [Official site](https://lanmessenger.github.io/) · [v1.3.27 release](https://github.com/lanmessenger/lanmessenger/releases/tag/v1.3.27) · [Asset list](https://github.com/lanmessenger/lanmessenger/releases/expanded_assets/v1.3.27)
- **Documented scope and gap.** Upstream describes automatic LAN discovery, direct files, local history, contact-list organization, broadcast to selected users or everyone, and communication over a reachable LAN while internet is unavailable. The source at the release tag emits a leave event on closing a group-mode chat window and saves history. The AES-256/RSA-2048 statement is a first-party algorithm claim. Room-wide file fan-out, per-member file completion, sender-independent pickup, group identity/key semantics and comparative security are unverified. The site's latency and throughput marketing lacks reproducible measurements in the cited evidence. [Project README](https://github.com/lanmessenger/lanmessenger#features) · [Official site](https://lanmessenger.github.io/#features) · [Tagged group close handler](https://github.com/lanmessenger/lanmessenger/blob/v1.3.27/src/gui/chat/chatroomwindow.cpp#L460-L472)

- **Source, history and release.** The pinned historical README describes unzip-and-run, private/group/broadcast chat, multiple file transfer, voice and bridging two LANs. GitHub's v4.0.1 release (14 May 2026) contains Windows x64 setup/ZIP, Linux x64 and Intel/ARM macOS archives. Its build workflow publishes the UI project. Runtime parity and the availability of every plugin or standalone bridge in every package remain unverified. [Historical README](https://github.com/hasankhan/Squiggle/blob/ef61dcc6169af47eb10e275e672d2114c43fdf7c/Readme.md) · [Tagged README](https://github.com/hasankhan/Squiggle/blob/v4.0.1/README.md) · [v4.0.1 assets](https://github.com/hasankhan/Squiggle/releases/expanded_assets/v4.0.1) · [Tagged release workflow](https://github.com/hasankhan/Squiggle/blob/v4.0.1/.github/workflows/release.yml#L39)

The tagged translation tool contains a Google Translate API client used in translation-file generation. Shipped in-chat translation and its default backend or offline behavior remain unverified. The tagged file handler opens the output stream when accepted. Current group attachment fan-out, per-member completion and offline custody are unverified. [Screenshot source](https://github.com/hasankhan/Squiggle/blob/v4.0.1/Squiggle.Screenshot/WindowsScreenCaptureService.cs#L62) · [Voice project](https://github.com/hasankhan/Squiggle/blob/v4.0.1/Squiggle.VoiceChat/Squiggle.VoiceChat.csproj) · [Translation tool](https://github.com/hasankhan/Squiggle/blob/v4.0.1/Squiggle.Translate/MainWindow.xaml.cs#L140) · [Google client](https://github.com/hasankhan/Squiggle/blob/v4.0.1/Squiggle.Translate/GoogleTranslator.cs#L38) · [File acceptance](https://github.com/hasankhan/Squiggle/blob/v4.0.1/Squiggle.FileTransfer/FileTransferHandler.cs#L56)

- **Availability.** The official legacy archive and SourceForge default identify 5.8.6 (13 February 2023) as stable. The main site describes version 6 as beta and its download page names 5.99.0, but the listed desktop packages and source tarball were marked Coming soon. The reviewed links did not establish public beta binary or mobile-store availability. The beta docs index mentions 5.9.2 while its compatibility detail link returns 404. The reviewed evidence leaves 5.9.2 release status and compatibility details unresolved. [Stable archive](https://www.beebeep.net/legacy/download) · [SourceForge files](https://sourceforge.net/projects/beebeep/files/) · [Beta site](https://www.beebeep.net/) · [Beta downloads](https://www.beebeep.net/download) · [Docs index](https://www.beebeep.net/docs)
- **Stable 5.x.** Legacy first-party material documents local groups, file/folder transfer and sharing, configurable defaults through \`beebeep.rc\`, voice messages in supported builds and desktop sharing. Its FAQ describes connection encryption and separately discloses online version checks and historical analytics attempts. The legacy site's popularity and superiority claims have no independently verifiable basis in the cited evidence. [Legacy product page](https://www.beebeep.net/legacy) · [Legacy downloads and voice exceptions](https://www.beebeep.net/legacy/download) · [Legacy help](https://www.beebeep.net/legacy/help#groups) · [Legacy FAQ](https://www.beebeep.net/legacy/faq)
- **6 beta group and files.** The project documents automatic local peer discovery, named groups, multiple admins, confirmation by default for 6 peers, a user opt-in to auto-accept contact invites, direct adding of 5.x peers, invite expiration, leave/removal and a pre-join history boundary. File fan-out gives each member a separate offer/progress item. An offline member can get a still-valid offer later. File bytes require direct reachability to the sender in the documented flow. The guide describes file-integrity checks and resume, mandatory acceptance for non-contacts and on public networks, conditional auto-download and a voice-message exception. Files above 1 MB normally wait for a network route over the documented Bluetooth path, with a smaller private photo copy as an exception. Mixed 5.x transfer is described as using older encryption. One blanket encryption or compatibility claim would overstate this evidence. [Beta overview](https://www.beebeep.net/) · [Groups](https://www.beebeep.net/docs/groups) · [Files](https://www.beebeep.net/docs/files)
- **6 beta live media.** Guides labeled from 6.0.0 describe a 1:1 voice call to a contact and live screen sharing from a desktop to one contact over a direct network connection. The screen guide explicitly excludes v5 for that specific v6 flow. It also describes a distinct screenshot send path. These are guide descriptions. Shipping platform parity and behavior under interruption remain untested. [Voice calls](https://www.beebeep.net/docs/calls) · [Screen sharing](https://www.beebeep.net/docs/screen-sharing)
- **Mesh Talk applicability.** Compare individual recipient progress, explicit public-network consent, clear offer expiry, and operator defaults. Mesh Talk already has receiving policies and can serve retained bytes from authorized peers or a configured post office. Measure whether the UI distinguishes a queued offer, accepted transfer, verified saved bytes and resumable custody. Saved the first-party research in [req-029-lan-sources.md](/Users/kingsonwu/programming/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/.worktrees/req-029/tmp/req-029-lan-sources.md). It covers all five products, with source URLs, release status, product gaps, and implications for Mesh Talk.

- **LANChat v0.1.5** ships a host-dependent browser client with image and file workflows. PWA installation, independent browser discovery, and live media remain unverified. [Release](https://github.com/cap153/LANChat/releases/tag/v0.1.5) · [Web server source](https://github.com/cap153/LANChat/blob/v0.1.5/src-tauri/src/web_server.rs)
- **BLIP** ships desktop WebRTC calling and screen sharing. Group voice channels use a host-centered topology. GitHub marks 2.0.3 as Latest and 3.0.0 as a prerelease. Its public website is a static showcase. [Architecture](https://github.com/krwg/blip/blob/v2.0.3/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) · [Releases](https://github.com/krwg/blip/releases) · [Website](https://krwg.github.io/blip/)
- **LAN Messenger** lists 1.3.27 on both its official site and GitHub. **Squiggle** publishes macOS and Linux packages, with media plugin parity still unverified. **BeeBEEP** lists 5.8.6 as stable, while its v6 beta download page marks packages as coming soon. [LAN Messenger](https://lanmessenger.github.io/) · [Squiggle](https://github.com/hasankhan/Squiggle/releases/tag/v4.0.1) · [BeeBEEP stable](https://www.beebeep.net/legacy/download) · [BeeBEEP beta](https://www.beebeep.net/download)

The review used public sources and tagged code. Runtime behavior, interoperability, and performance remain untested.

**English note**

- **Original** “Give URLs, product gaps, applicability.”
- **Better** “Include source links, identify product gaps, and explain what applies to Mesh Talk.”
- **Why** Parallel verbs make each deliverable clear, and naming Mesh Talk gives “applicability” a concrete target.
- **Useful pattern** “For each product, cite the evidence and explain how it applies to our use case.”
- **Collocations** cite primary sources, identify product gaps, assess applicability.
